entities.label: Idea
entities.summary:
Nazism, or National Socialism, was a virulent fascist, antisemitic, and totalitarian political ideology that dominated Germany from 1933 to 1945 under Adolf Hitler and the National Socialist German Workers' Party (NSDAP). It rejected liberal democracy, communism, and internationalism, instead championing an ethnically pure 'Volksgemeinschaft' (people's community) rooted in a pseudo-scientific racial hierarchy that placed Aryan Germans at its apex and Jews, Romani, Slavs, and others at its nadir. Its rise, fueled by post-World War I grievances, economic instability, and a potent cult of personality around Hitler, fundamentally reshaped 20th-century geopolitical landscapes and plunged the world into its deadliest conflict.

Upon seizing power in January 1933, the Nazi regime swiftly dismantled democratic institutions, suppressed dissent through the Gestapo and concentration camps, and initiated a systematic persecution of Jews, culminating in the Nuremberg Laws of 1935. The regime aggressively pursued rearmament, violating the Treaty of Versailles, and embarked on an expansionist foreign policy that led to the annexation of Austria (Anschluss) in 1938 and Czechoslovakia's Sudetenland, culminating in the invasion of Poland on September 1, 1939, igniting World War II. During the war, the Nazis implemented the "Final Solution," an industrial-scale genocide that murdered approximately six million Jews and millions of others deemed 'undesirable' across occupied Europe.
